arch_opening: There is an update available — version 2.3.0, and one part of it is critical. Anthropic published 'The New Rules of Context Engineering for Claude 5 Generation Models' on 2026-07-24, reporting that they deleted over 80% of Claude Code's system prompt with no measurable loss on coding evals, and naming conflicting instructions across layers as the failure mode that had crept in. This release applies that to us. Three things: a new `scripts/check-handoff.sh` that mechanically checks a brief or review request is complete before anyone builds or reviews against it — that is the critical one, because RULES.md now calls it as a gate command; the five-rule Token Rules block replaced with the cost model it was standing in for; and the token-optimizer skill de-duplicated, because the copy your agents actually load had drifted and was missing the cost model, the cache setting, and the model routing table. I'll check what applies to your setup.

changes.title: scripts/check-handoff.sh — a bounced step is the most expensive event in this methodology
changes.what_changed: New framework-owned script `scripts/check-handoff.sh brief|review-request|review-feedback`, shipped in both template sets and the Codex build. It asserts the handoff file has its sections, has no unfilled template placeholders, and — for a brief — that the Definition of Done carries a runnable command in backticks. RULES.md's Mechanical Gate gains a `scripts/check-handoff.sh brief` row. The Architect runs it as the eighth and last line of the Pre-Flight Check; the Builder runs `brief` at session start before writing code; the Reviewer runs `review-request` as their first act, before reading anything. The ARCHITECT-BRIEF template's Definition of Done now requires a command.
changes.old_behavior: The brief contract was prose asserted in three places — BUILDER.md ('a complete brief has: decisions, build order, an Out of Scope section, flags, and a Definition of Done'), the ARCHITECT.md brief template, and playbooks/BRIEF-EXAMPLES.md. Nothing checked it. An incomplete brief was discovered by the Builder partway through a step, or by the Reviewer at review time — after the context had already been spent.
changes.new_behavior: One command, run at three points, catches a missing Out of Scope section or an unrunnable Definition of Done before anyone spends a context window on it. A Definition of Done you cannot write as a command means the step is not specified sharply enough to build — surfaced at brief time for one line instead of at review time for a whole loop.
changes.user_impact_plain: A bounced step re-runs the Reviewer, the Builder fix, and the Architect re-brief — re-billing every agent's accumulated context across the whole loop. It is the most expensive thing that happens in this methodology, and it costs far more than every file read in a project's lifetime. This is a token optimization wearing a quality-control hat.
changes.how_to_assess: Check whether `scripts/check-handoff.sh` exists in the project root. If not, this release must be installed as a unit — the RULES.md gate row and the role-file instructions all call it, and installing those without the script gives the project a gate command that fails on every step. Then check the Builder and Reviewer role files' Session Start and the Architect's Pre-Flight for the three call sites, and the ARCHITECT-BRIEF template's Definition of Done section for the required-command wording.
changes.user_decision: Want me to install the handoff check and wire it into your RULES.md gate, your Pre-Flight, and the Builder/Reviewer session starts? This is the critical part of the release — the script and the files that call it have to land together.

changes.title: The five-rule Token Rules block is gone — replaced by the cost model it stood in for
changes.what_changed: The Token Rules block ('Trust it. Skip the file read. / Kill the tool call. / Parallelize them. / Route to subagent. / Delete it.') is removed from every instruction file — CLAUDE.md, both template sets' BUILDER.md and REVIEWER.md, the Codex AGENTS.md and SKILL.md, and the token-optimizer skill. In its place: a short statement of why context costs what it does, a Gotchas section, and one role-specific line per subagent (their context cap). METHODOLOGY.md and the README section were rewritten to match.
changes.old_behavior: Every role recited five imperative rules at session start, and Builder and Reviewer loaded the identical block twice — once from CLAUDE.md, once from their own role file (the v2.2.0 inline-block design). Two of the five were actively harmful: 'Is this in a skill or memory? Trust it. Skip the file read.' instructs an agent to act on state that may be stale, contradicting the memory system's own contract that memories are point-in-time observations. 'Output > 20 lines you won't use → Route to subagent' sets a threshold below the cost of spawning a subagent, so following it literally raises spend.
changes.new_behavior: What remains is written as reasons rather than commands, stated once. Current models already parallelize calls, skip speculative reads, and avoid restating the prompt — rules for those cost tokens every session and change nothing. The rules that were load-bearing survive in the skill as judgment framing: verify file:line before acting on a memory, grep before read because unneeded lines get re-billed every turn, filter bash output at the call site, route a genuinely large verification to a throwaway subagent.
changes.user_impact_plain: This reverses a call v2.2.0 made deliberately. v2.2.0 kept rule duplication on the strength of prompt-repetition research, reasoning that point-of-use repetition was accuracy-safe. Anthropic's 2026-07-24 article supersedes that for Claude 5 generation models: repetition across layers is now the named defect, and the internal failure they cite is conflicting instructions in exactly this shape. Our own repo had already produced that failure — see the skill de-duplication below. The second half of v2.2.0's reasoning still holds, so each subagent keeps its context cap inline in its own role file.
changes.how_to_assess: Grep the user's CLAUDE.md, BUILDER.md, and REVIEWER.md for 'Kill the tool call'. If present, they are carrying the block — and if it appears in both CLAUDE.md and a role file, the subagent is carrying it twice in one context. Offer the replacement, preserving their personas and any project-specific rules they have added. If the user has deliberately kept the block after reading this reasoning, leave it: it is not broken, only redundant.
changes.user_decision: Want me to replace the Token Rules block with the cost model and gotchas? Note this reverses a v2.2.0 design decision — the harmful 'trust it, skip the file read' rule goes away either way, so I can do just that part if you'd rather keep the rest.

changes.title: The token-optimizer copy your agents load had drifted and was missing the cost model
changes.what_changed: `docs/token-optimization.md`, `templates/project-folder/.claude/skills/token-optimization.md`, and `codex-skill/references/token-optimization.md` are now one byte-identical file, enforced by a new entry in `scripts/check-consistency.sh`'s identical-copy audit — the same mechanism that already guards RULES.md and the playbooks.
changes.old_behavior: The shipped skill was a stale fork of the docs copy. It was missing three sections: the 94.6% cost model ('what you carry, not what you load'), the ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H cache setting, and the model routing table. CLAUDE.md instructs every role to load that skill first, before anything else — so the framework's highest-value guidance sat in the one file nobody was told to read, and had done since v2.0.0 added those sections to only one of the copies.
changes.new_behavior: One source, three identical copies, and the repo self-audit fails if they drift again.
changes.user_impact_plain: This is what unchecked duplication does, and it is why the release above removes the rest of it. The fix costs nothing and the sections it restores are the ones that actually move the bill.
changes.how_to_assess: Read the user's `.claude/skills/token-optimization.md`. If it has no 'What Actually Costs Money' or 'Cache TTL' section, they are on the stale copy. Refreshing it is safe — it is framework-owned and carries no project-specific content. While there, check `~/.claude/settings.json` for ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H: on a measured session the missing setting cost $25 of a $114 day, and it is the single cheapest win available.
changes.user_decision: Want me to refresh your token-optimizer skill to the current version? Nothing project-specific lives in that file.
